newsitem.title: USA: Alaska volcano eruption continues at low level.
newsitem.headline: Alaska volcano eruption continues at low level.

text.p: Okmok Volcano, a 3,250-foot (990-metre) peak on Alaska's Umnak Island, has been spewing lava, ash and steam since it began erupting last week, officials from the Alaska Volcano Observatory said on Thursday.

"It's been pretty much continuous since the beginning of the eruption last Thursday morning, but with various intensities of lava flow from the cone," Terry Keith, scientist-in-charge at the Alaska Volcano Observatory said.
"There is intermittent steam with some ash bursts from this eruption around the volcano," Keith said. "It's really a pretty small thing right now."

The most powerful recent eruption on the Aleutian island appeared to be the one that occurred on Tuesday morning, which sent ash up to between 10,000 and 15,000 feet (3,000 and 4,500 metres) in the air, the observatory said.

Keith said no ash fall has been reported in any of the nearby settlements, which include the tiny Aleut village of Nikolski, about 45 (70 km) miles west of Okmok, and Unalaska, about 75 miles (120 km) southwest of the volcano.

Okmok Volcano is about 875 miles (1,400 km) southwest of Anchorage. It has a six-mile-(10 km) wide caldera that occupies most of the eastern end of Umnak Island. Lava, ash and steam have been emitted from a cone at the 2,500-foot (760-metre) level of the volcano in the current series of eruptions, the observatory said.
Okmok has had frequent and sporadic but relatively weak eruptions, the observatory said. The last eruptive period lasted from November 1986 to February 1988.
